name: Conductors within one cable
summary: An outline or loop drawn across several conductor lines to show that they are cores of the same cable.
description: On multi-line schematics each core is drawn as a separate line, which hides the fact that several of them share one sheath. A grouping outline drawn across those lines tells the reader they are cores of one cable. It is typically paired with a cable tag so that the cores can be traced to the cable schedule.

The outline implies no screen and no particular core count beyond the lines it crosses. Spare cores are often not drawn, so the cable may have more cores than the outline encloses. Cores from one cable may also be split across several sheets, each with its own grouping mark and the same cable tag.
readingNotes: Read the cable tag beside the grouping outline.
Expect spare cores that are not drawn.
drawingChecklist: Tag every grouping outline with the cable number.
Use the same tag on every sheet the cable appears on.
Record spare cores in the cable schedule.
distinction: A grouping outline shows shared sheath only; a screen outline shows a conductive shield around the cores.
